title: Toxic alcohols — methanol / ethylene glycol (e.g. antifreeze) poisoning
population: Adults and children (one pathway; ADULT / CHILD and METHANOL / EG lines where they differ)
dagger_note: † = clinical or local addition, not in the SA guideline
item_format: t=text, s=source:printed page, d=dagger, b=bold, k=kind (check|value|yn|info|sub), h=heading

items.t: History of ingestion of a methanol or ethylene glycol product (list below) — container seen
Toxic-alcohol toxidrome: inebriation / depressed LOC, nausea, vomiting, high anion gap metabolic acidosis, hyperventilation
METHANOL: visual disturbance (after a 12–24 h latent period)
EG: renal failure, hypocalcaemia (QT prolonged, tetany), oxalate crystals in urine
Early on the patient may look only "drunk".

items.h: Where these come from (check the container)

items.t: Ethylene glycol: radiator coolant / antifreeze; occasionally brake fluid; homemade toilet and drain cleaners
Ethylene glycol also: de-icers, hydraulic fluid
Methanol: stove or model fuels, antifreeze, windscreen washer fluid
Methanol also: home-brewed / counterfeit spirits, paint thinners, varnish removers, carburettor cleaner
SA methylated spirits no longer contains methanol

admission.title: Start ethanol antidote = history + any two

items.t: Urinary oxalate crystals (EG) or visual disturbance (methanol)

admission.title: Road to Health Booklet (child) / clinic card, previous records (adult)
Vitals and measurements
admission.note: Abnormal = outside age-appropriate norms or the patient's baseline

items.t: Value on arrival: pH ____ HCO₃ ____ Na ____ Cl ____
pH < 7.3 or HCO₃ < 20 (+ history): counts toward starting ethanol (§2)
Profound acidosis: REFER for early haemodialysis
Then 4-hourly on ethanol, and 1 h after each bicarbonate dose
Low HGT (toxic alcohol and ethanol effect): correct it
CHILD hypoglycaemic: dextrose 10% 2 mL/kg IV, then 10% dextrose maintenance

admission.title: Red flags to rule out on arrival

decision.t: 10. Severe → ethanol + bicarbonate, REFER for haemodialysis

11. ADMIT — PHC STG: refer all toxic-alcohol cases; start ethanol here before transfer. Stabilise, then continue on the 0 h – discharge inpatient chart and the 24-hour nursing record. No activated charcoal (ineffective for methanol / EG / ethanol).

chart.phase_note: Paeds STG has no toxic-alcohol section: CHILD antidote lines are extrapolated† — discuss with the Poisons Centre.

standing.t: Ethanol 20% rate, GCS, RR hourly (HR, BP hourly on the ward observation chart)
Urine output hourly (catheter if EG or oliguric)
VBG 4-hourly and 1 h after each bicarbonate dose
Aspiration precautions: head up, side-lying if drowsy
Never give commercial ethanol IV · no activated charcoal

rows.label: 0 h
rows.lead: Check the referral note for ethanol or bicarbonate already given — do not duplicate. Consult the Poisons Helpline 0861 555 777 / UFS 082 491 0160. Treat early. Arrange referral for haemodialysis now if severe.

feed.t: Start if history + any two: pH < 7.3 · HCO₃ < 20 mmol/L · oxalate crystals (EG) / visual disturbance (methanol)
METHANOL + acidosis or visual disturbance: start immediately
Ethanol 96%: 1 part + 4 parts juice/water (250 mL + 1000 mL = 1250 mL)
Or spirits 40–43% (gin, whisky, vodka): 1 + 1 (500 mL + 500 mL)

feed.h: Give orally, or by NGT if not cooperative

feed.t: Maintenance: non-drinker 0.5 mL/kg/h; chronic drinker 1 mL/kg/h
60 kg: load 240 mL; then 30 mL/h (non-drinker) or 60 mL/h (drinker)
CHILD: same mL/kg regimen — confirm with Poisons Centre; HGT hourly

tests.t: VBG: pH, HCO₃, Na, Cl → anion gap
Methanol / EG / ethanol levels usually unavailable: titrate to acidosis
If female of child-bearing age: urine βhCG
Record time of ingestion on the request form

treatment.t: Protect airway; depressed LOC may need ventilation → REFER
Seizures: status epilepticus protocol
ADULT: sodium bicarbonate 8.4% 50–100 mmol IV over 30–45 min
CHILD: sodium bicarbonate 8.4% 1 mL/kg IV over 1 h (Paeds STG salicylate dose)
Correct severe or clinically evident hypocalcaemia first — rapid correction of acidosis can precipitate seizures
Correct hypoglycaemia; CHILD: dextrose 10% 2 mL/kg IV, then 10% dextrose maintenance
Thiamine 100 mg oral daily · pyridoxine 100 mg oral daily
CHILD: dose via Poisons Centre
No activated charcoal (ineffective)
Severe with profound acidosis: REFER for early haemodialysis
Ethanol running during transfer; send solution and rate
Others drank the same product: find and assess them

feed.t: Too drowsy: reduce rate, protect airway

treatment.t: Referral / haemodialysis discussed? Poisons Centre advice noted

feed.t: Titrate the rate to improvement in acidosis and systemic toxicity

treatment.t: Still acidotic: repeat bicarbonate; recheck calcium first
Worsening acidosis despite ethanol + bicarbonate: REFER for haemodialysis
Urine output falling (EG): renal failure → REFER for dialysis

feed.t: Continue. Do not stop because the patient looks well.

treatment.t: New acidosis or visual disturbance = methanol toxicity: ethanol + evaluate urgent dialysis
Thiamine + pyridoxine daily (ADULT)

feed.t: Several days of ethanol may be needed, until the clinical condition improves

treatment.t: Intentional: once medically stable, mental health assessment (suicide risk); refer social / psychological / psychiatric services
CHILD: home circumstances; safe-storage counselling
Acidosis resolved and clinically improved: stop ethanol, then recheck VBG after 6–12 h
Acidosis returns off ethanol: restart ethanol, discuss dialysis with Poisons Centre
Discharge criteria · letter · eye / renal follow-up booked

items.t: Indication: history + any two of pH < 7.3, HCO₃ < 20 mmol/L, oxalate crystals (EG) / visual disturbance (methanol)
96% ethanol: 1 part + 4 parts juice or water
40% spirits: 1 + 1; SA spirits are often 43% — use the same way
Maintenance: non-drinker 0.5 mL/kg/h · chronic drinker 1 mL/kg/h
Target ethanol level 1–1.3 g/L; if levels unavailable, titrate to acidosis and signs of toxicity
Commercial ethanol is not for IV use
CHILD: same mL/kg regimen; watch HGT
ADULT: sodium bicarbonate 8.4% 50–100 mmol IV over 30–45 min
CHILD: 8.4% 1 mL/kg IV over 1 h (Paeds STG salicylate dose)
Correct severe or clinically evident hypocalcaemia before rapid acidosis correction (seizure risk)
CHILD: dextrose 10% 2 mL/kg IV, then 10% maintenance; persistent: REFER
Thiamine 100 mg oral daily; pyridoxine 100 mg oral daily
Severe poisoning with profound acidosis — early dialysis is the treatment of choice
Acidosis not improving on ethanol + bicarbonate
PHC STG: refer all toxic-alcohol cases
GCS falling / too drowsy on ethanol: reduce rate, protect airway

discharge.title: Discharge criteria — all must be met (conditional items where they apply)

items.t: Acidosis resolved; off ethanol ≥ 24 h without recurrence
METHANOL: vision documented; eye referral if any deficit
EG: creatinine improving; renal follow-up plan
Intentional: mental health assessment and plan
CHILD: home circumstances assessed, safe storage counselled
Cluster from home brew: others traced, reported
METHANOL with visual symptoms: eye clinic
Return at once: drowsiness, fast breathing, vomiting, blurred vision, little urine

nursing.title: 24-hour nursing record — ethanol antidote, HGT, GCS, breathing, urine
nursing.period: One sheet per 24 hours while on ethanol; hourly rows, heavier rule every 4 h

items.t: Oral or NGT only — never IV
Record the rate every hour and any change the doctor makes
Record when the load was given; bicarbonate doses in Notes
GCS and RR (deep, fast breathing = acidosis) hourly
HR, BP hourly on the ward observation chart
Drowsy: head up / side-lying, watch for vomiting
Urine output hourly (catheter if EG or oliguric)
METHANOL: vision 4-hourly — count fingers / blurred / normal
Note the time each VBG is drawn

call.t: GCS falling or too drowsy on ethanol
